insight.title: The Focal Distortion
insight.subtitle: Why your focus creates a false reality.

sections.text: Ever wondered why a minor inconvenience can ruin an entire morning? Your brain is a spotlight, not a camera. It illuminates a single detail until that detail feels like your entire reality.
This is the Focusing Illusion. We mistake the intensity of our attention for the importance of the object. When you stare at a problem, you aren't measuring its size; you're just magnifying it.
From a typo in a report to a slow driver, small frictions feel massive because they consume your bandwidth. You aren’t reacting to the event; you are reacting to the space it occupies.
Try this today: When you feel frustrated, look at the furthest physical object in your sight for three seconds. This "optical zoom out" forces your brain to acknowledge a larger, more accurate world.
You aren't experiencing the world; you are experiencing where you choose to look.
Notice how many "emergencies" simply disappear the moment you stop looking directly at them.

news.title: Oil rises as Trump reaffirms deadline for striking Iran's power plants, bridges
news.description: Crude prices ticked higher after Trump repeated the Tuesday deadline for escalating attacks on Iran's power plants and bridges.
news.why: Your electricity and heating bills may rise if energy infrastructure is destroyed.

news.title: Iran War: Trump Says Reopening Hormuz Must Be Part of Ceasefire Deal
news.description: President Donald Trump insisted that freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz be part of any deal to end the Middle East war and escalated threats to obliterate key Iranian infrastructure if his terms aren’t met before a Tuesday deadline.
news.why: Blocked shipping routes could make your online orders and groceries more expensive.

news.title: Iran rejects ceasefire, wants permanent end to war
news.description: 'Aggressors will see our might,' says Iran Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi
news.why: Continued fighting may lead to slower global hiring and fewer job opportunities.

news.title: Inside Iran’s 10-point proposal: Demands and offers to end war as Trump sets Tuesday deadline
news.description: Iran has pushed back against a ceasefire push, laying out a 10-point proposal that calls for a permanent end to the war, removal of sanctions, and guarantees against future attacks. In return, it has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — but with a $2 million fee per ship.
news.why: Rigid peace conditions suggest your cost of living will remain high.

news.title: Number of U.S. Service Members Injured in Trump’s War Rises
news.description: The number of injured troops continues to rise as Trump’s war continues.
news.why: Growing military involvement could lead to higher defense taxes and security changes.

news.title: 'If I had my choice...': Trump eyes Iran's oil, tells the world he is a 'businessman' first
news.description: President Donald Trump indicated the US could seize Iranian oil amid escalating West Asia tensions. He referenced business dealings and the concept of spoils of war. Trump also criticized allies like Japan, Australia, and South Korea for their lack of support. He praised Saudi Arabia, Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait for their assistance.
news.why: Changes in global oil ownership could shift your long-term transport costs.

news.title: NASA mission flying by far side of moon
news.description: There will be a temporary communications blackout as the spacecraft passes behind the moon, which is expected and planned. Follow for live updates.
news.why: Advancing space exploration will eventually improve your GPS and global communication.
